summary:
ASTROHEALTH is an interactive prototype of a crew health system for long-duration spaceflight: one place where a mission’s medical team can see how its astronauts are actually holding up.

Deep-space missions remove what terrestrial medicine depends on — a hospital. On a 148-day lunar transit, microgravity, radiation and disrupted sleep act on the body continuously, while the crew sits further from definitive care than anyone has ever been. Monitoring alone does not solve this; by the time a number looks wrong, the problem already exists.

Our prototype brings eight vital signs into a single mission dashboard, then adds the layers monitoring cannot provide: a Simulation Lab that rehearses five deterioration scenarios, ASTRA AI that surfaces risk trends early, a timed Emergency Response drill with escalation protocol and incident logging, habitat-to-health correlation, a crew-wide Mission Control view, and automatic medical report generation.

All data is simulated, and every insight is presented as a signal for human clinicians — never a diagnosis. ASTROHEALTH supports a medical team’s judgement rather than replacing it.

Crew health is the limiting factor on how far we can go.
details:
What ASTROHEALTH does

ASTROHEALTH (ASTRA-MED 360) is an eight-module crew health system for long-duration spaceflight, built around a fictional mission — ARTEMIS-X 042, day 148 of a lunar transfer orbit, with a three-person crew.

Main Dashboard — Eight vital signs in one view: heart rate, blood oxygen, body temperature, hydration, blood pressure, respiratory rate, stress and sleep quality, consolidated into an overall health score with a biometric trend chart and a running status feed.

Health Simulation Lab — Five selectable scenarios (normal health, oxygen emergency, high heart rate, dehydration risk, extreme fatigue). The user starts a scenario and watches vitals shift and the system react, in a controlled test environment.

ASTRA AI Analysis — A predictive risk layer reporting current risk level, detected abnormalities, trend prediction and recommended action, with an “Explain Risk Insight” function. A Signal Integrity panel reports model confidence, data quality and sensor coverage, so the user can judge how much to trust the output.

Emergency Response — A timed escalation drill: critical alert, affected astronaut’s abnormal signals, a four-step recommended protocol, a live event timeline, a two-minute response countdown, communication status, and automatic incident documentation.

Astronaut Body Scan — Anatomical visualisation across five systems, linking each to the relevant vital-sign trend.

Space Environment — Habitat conditions (microgravity exposure, radiation, sleep disruption, activity, cabin temperature and oxygen) mapped against crew health indicators.

Mission Control Center — All three crew members side by side with status, vitals and comms, plus a mission timeline and medical-team alert log.

Medical Report Generator — Daily, weekly and incident reports, exportable for mission records.

How it works

Vital-sign data enters the dashboard and is scored against normal ranges. ASTRA AI reads the trend rather than the single reading, so a value drifting toward a threshold is flagged while it is still within normal limits. If a scenario crosses into emergency, the Emergency Response module converts the alert into a structured protocol with a timeline and an auto-generated incident report. The Space Environment module runs alongside, correlating habitat conditions with crew indicators to help explain why a trend is moving.

Benefits

Monitoring alone is reactive — by the time a number reads abnormal, the problem exists. ASTROHEALTH adds three things monitoring cannot: early trend detection, rehearsal before a real emergency, and automatic documentation during one, when crew attention is scarcest. Mission Control view extends this from one astronaut to a whole crew.

What we hope to achieve

To demonstrate that crew health on deep-space missions can be made continuously visible and actionable, and to develop the prototype toward real sensor input, validated risk models and clinical review.

Safety framing

All data is simulated. ASTRA AI outputs are risk signals, not medical diagnoses, and human medical teams remain responsible for assessment and response.
